To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a single, end-to-end neural network model to perform boundary identification, entity typing and relation classification and that we demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves better end-to-end performance than all previous joint modelling approaches.

(i) joint modelling of all three tasks of end-to-end relation identification leads to better performance, (ii) neural networks based joint models are better than the traditional CRF based models and (iii) Markov Logic Networks based inference can further boost the performance of the joint models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an effective end-to-end approach for relation extraction using neural networks and Markov logic networks.

we have proposed a novel approach for end-to-end relation classification which is better than the existing joint approaches and also has a better performance than the state of the art pipeline approach.
joint modelling of all tasks is better than separate modelling of each task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve better end-to-end performance by using a single joint model than by using a pipeline of multiple models.
it is possible to achieve better end-to-end results by jointly modelling all the three tasks using a single neural network based model.
joint modelling can be used to achieve better end-to-end performance than separate predictive models in a “pipeline”, even when the joint models do not use any additional domain knowledge.
